artifacts.summary: Re-measures all seven in-scope suites (all now 0-failure standalone), confirms dependencies 423/445 are closed and task 568 already fixed one shared-cause suite, finds a new concurrency-dependent flake in test-gate-lock.sh under run-all.sh's own aggregate battery, confirms the excluded eighth suite's fixture-not-clean symptom still reproduces after 423's closure, and flags two stale known-failures.txt rows.

memory_candidates.content: Task-number references embedded in an /orchestrate dispatch description (e.g. "open record 423", "open record 445") can go stale between dispatch generation and execution if the referenced task closes in the interim -- always re-check a cited task's live status (active_projects vs. specs/archive/) before treating a dispatch's framing of it as a blocker or as an unresolved recipient for a hand-off. An archived task cannot receive new findings; a 'hand this observation to record N' instruction against a now-closed N needs a fresh follow-up task instead.

A suite that passes standalone can still fail only inside run-all.sh's own aggregate/parallel battery -- run a cheap `run-all.sh --only <suite1,suite2,...> --fail-on-new` smoke test across a task's declared file_scope suites before assuming standalone green means Gate 8 green. This surfaced a genuine ambient-host-state timing flake in test-gate-lock.sh (passes 16/0 alone, fails 14/2 in the aggregate) that no standalone run would ever reveal.

claim_invalidations.claim: Task 423 closed 2026-11-10 ([COMPLETED]); the dispatch description's framing of it as an open blocking dependency for test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh is superseded, and its own closure attributes a different root cause (gate-24 /ide findings) than the fixture-not-clean symptom this task's description separately reports, which this dispatch independently re-confirmed still reproduces after 423's closure.

Task 445 closed 2026-11-10 ([COMPLETED]) and delivered the EXPECTED/NEW distinction mechanism (gate8_run()'s three-way verdict, run-all.sh --fail-on-new, known-failures.txt) outcome 4 names as a dependency to wait on; it is no longer a blocker and was used directly in this dispatch's own verification.

The dispatch description's carried failure counts (test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh 5 failed, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion.sh 3 failed, and report 01's earlier 12/2/11/7-failure figures for these five suites) are refuted by direct re-run in this dispatch: all five now report 0 failed standalone (29, 17, 312, 37, and 21 passed respectively).
